Dear Ms. Whitaker,

My name is Gregory Hall, and I am the chairman of the County Historical Society. I am writing about the new rule that the City Central Library started on March 1st. Now, people must pay $75 an hour to look at the old maps from before 1900. I think this fee is unfair, and I hope the library will think about changing it.

For ten years, I have been studying the history of our waterfront area. I always handle the old maps with great care, and I have never damaged one.

I think the fee is a problem for most people in our community. A university professor may have grant money to pay it, but a local writer or a volunteer usually does not. It seems that the library is now making it easier for university researchers than for ordinary residents.

Last week, I spoke with Mr. James Miller, the deputy librarian. He told me the fee is needed to take care of the maps. However, our taxes already pay for keeping these maps safe and dry. I also do not understand why we should pay extra just to sit in the reading room, where a staff member is always watching. Yesterday, I saw two high school students leave the library because they could not pay the fee for their history project. That was very sad to see.

I have a suggestion. Could the library offer a free pass to local residents who are working on community history projects, not business projects? I would also like the Library Board to review the fee at its next meeting.

Please let me know how the library decided on the $75 amount. I would also like to know whether the public could have some free hours each week to use the maps.

Thank you for your time. I look forward to your reply.

Sincerely,
Gregory Hall
Chairman, County Historical Society
